sentences.text: Lophorhothon is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous of Alabama, and possibly Georgia and North Carolina. The name Lophorhothon means "crested nose", derived from Greek words for crested and nose.
The specific epithet atopus comes from the Greek word atopos, meaning "uncommon" or "strange".
The juvenile holotype specimen is estimated to be 4.5 meters long, which is small for a hadrosaur.
Adult Lophorhothon are estimated to have been as large as Hadrosaurus, Hypsibema, Kritosaurus, and Gryposaurus.
Remains of Lophorhothon were first discovered during the 1940s.
The genus Lophorhothon was named by Wann Langston in 1960.
A more complete specimen of Lophorhothon was unearthed in Alabama in 2021.
The holotype specimen was likely transported by a river and buried in silty carbonate sediments of the Mississippi embayment.
A 2010 analysis indicated Lophorhothon was a basal member of the Hadrosauroidea.
Lophorhothon is classified within the family Hadrosauridae.
Lophorhothon is classified within the subfamily Saurolophinae.
Lophorhothon lived from the Santonian to the Campanian stages, approximately 85.7 to 72.2 million years ago.
Lophorhothon lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
Some researchers have suggested that the material may represent a juvenile Prosaurolophus.
In 1998, James Lamb suggested the genus might represent a basal iguanodont, an idea that did not gain widespread acceptance.
